---
title: "Column layouts"
---

What each column of each Martinec et al. (2018) data file holds, for the
archives first received (`benchmarkA/`, `benchmarkB/`) and for the set Martinec
sent in September 2026 (`resultsA_2026/` to `resultsE_2026/`). Every file is
named by its path under `data/original/`, because the same filename holds
different data in different directories.

Most of these files have no header. The only surviving record of their
contents is the GMT 4 script that drew the published figure, in lines like

```
awk '{print $1, -$4}' $inpSK | psxy -R -JX $lineSK -K -O >> pom.ps
```

which says: for that contributor, take column 1 as the abscissa and the
negation of column 4 as the ordinate, on whichever panel is being drawn. The
panel's y-axis label names the quantity.

GMT 4 no longer runs. This table is produced by
`scripts/decode_gmt_layouts.py`, which reads those scripts and writes down
what they say while the result can still be checked against the figures
shipped beside them.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Read the sign from here, never by assumption

Contributors do not agree on the sign of the geoid, and two of them submitted
the gravitational potential instead, which the scripts divide by the surface
gravity 9.8155. A reader that guesses is wrong by a factor of minus one for
six of the ten benchmark A contributors and by a factor of 9.8155 for two.
:::

## Panels

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
import json, pathlib
d = json.loads((pathlib.Path("../..") / "gia_mip" / "resources"
                / "column_layouts.json").read_text())
rows = ["| Script | Panel | Quantity | Series drawn |", "| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |"]
for s in d["scripts"]:
    for p in s["panels"]:
        drawn = sum(1 for x in p["series"] if x["drawn"])
        rows.append(f"| `{s['script']}` | {p['panel']} | {p['quantity']} | {drawn} |")
Markdown("\n".join(rows))
```

## By file

Each row says: in this script and panel, this quantity is column *n* of this
file, negated or not, with any arithmetic the script applies before plotting.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
import json, pathlib
d = json.loads((pathlib.Path("../..") / "gia_mip" / "resources"
                / "column_layouts.json").read_text())
out = []
for name, entries in d["by_file"].items():
    if name.startswith("<unresolved"):
        continue
    out.append(f"### `{name}`\n")
    out.append("| Script | Panel | Quantity | x | y | Sign | Arithmetic | In the figure |")
    out.append("| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |")
    for e in entries:
        y = e["ordinate"]
        extra = ""
        if e.get("value"):
            extra = f" (value: column {e['value'].get('column')})"
        out.append(
            f"| `{e['script']}` | {e['panel']} | {e['quantity']}{extra} | "
            f"{e['abscissa'].get('column', '?')} | {y.get('column', '?')} | "
            f"{'negated' if y.get('negated') else 'as stored'} | "
            f"{y.get('scale') or '-'} | "
            f"{'yes' if e['drawn_in_the_published_figure'] else 'commented out'} |")
    out.append("")
Markdown("\n".join(out))
```

## Time-series units

The time-series scripts of cases C, D and E say which column they plot and the
factor they apply, but not the unit the column is stored in, and the
contributors use different units: ice mass in kg, 1e17 kg or 1e18 kg, ocean
area as a fraction, a percentage or ten times a fraction. The table below is
transcribed from the file headers and from arithmetic on the files, with the
evidence for each entry. `si_factor` converts the stored value to kg, to a
fraction of 4 pi, or to metres. `tests/test_layouts.py` checks every factor
against the scale the script applies and the unit on the axis, so an entry
that disagrees with the published figure fails a test. See correction
`martinec2018-time-series-units`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
import json, pathlib
d = json.loads((pathlib.Path("../..") / "gia_mip" / "resources"
                / "column_layouts.json").read_text())
rows = ["| File | Time column | Column | Holds | Stored unit | si_factor | Evidence |",
        "| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | --- |"]
for path, entry in d["time_series_columns"].items():
    for column, c in sorted(entry["columns"].items(), key=lambda kv: int(kv[0])):
        rows.append(f"| `{path}` | {entry['time_column']} | {column} | `{c['name']}` | "
                    f"{c['units']} | {c['si_factor']:g} | {c.get('evidence', 'VEGA header')} |")
Markdown("\n".join(rows))
```

## Converted data

`gia_mip.benchmarks.martinec2018` reads every curve that a script draws, with
the column, sign and scale from this page and the fixes from
[the corrections](../data/corrections.qmd), and writes one NetCDF4 file per
case to `data/converted/martinec2018/`. Run `scripts/convert_martinec2018.py`
after `scripts/decode_gmt_layouts.py`. The module docstring describes the
groups and attributes of the output.

## What is not decoded

The Spada et al. (2011) archive holds 87 further GMT scripts covering its ten
tests. They are not decoded yet. Eleven README files inside the `T02`
directories do document the VILMA submissions: `u` is vertical displacement,
`v` is horizontal, `e` is geoid, in metres and metres per year, with `*cost`
holding the fine grid, `*costg` the global grid, and both poles omitted.
